title: Capacity Compositor: Unified GPU Pool Control Surface
creator: Ana Morales
description: Design and prototype a single control surface for Dedicated GPU pools that surfaces health diagnostics, autoscaling policy editing, burst controls, and real-time cost impact. The 'Capacity Compositor' groups metrics, editable policies, and action controls to reduce cognitive overhead for SREs and platform engineers managing reserved capacity.
goals: Provide a scannable overview of pool health across latency, utilization, and error rate
Allow safe edits to autoscale policies with inline simulation of cost and latency impact
Expose a bounded burst orchestration flow that shows available burst credits and projected costs
Reduce time to diagnose degraded pools by surfacing suggested remediation actions and links to logs/PRs
constraints: Must work inside current Console grid; header real estate is limited
Data latencies: health signals update at ~10s, cost simulations must be near-instant with cached estimates
Access controls: certain controls must be hidden/disabled for non-admin roles
Maintain parity with Dedicated API (no server-side changes required for v1 of UI)
decisions: Use a compact sparkline matrix for health (latency, GPU util, queue depth, errors) instead of large charts to allow multiple pools on a single page
Autoscale editor will be a staged modal with three tabs: Policy, Simulation, Review to prevent accidental commits
Burst control exposed as a slider with explicit credit/budget guardrail and an 'Instant test' button to run a simulated burst impact
Cost impact bar uses tokenized microchips to visually tie decisions to estimated monthly $/hour spend
accessibility_considerations: Ensure color contrast for health statuses meets WCAG AA
Keyboard operability for autoscale modal and burst slider; value labels exposed to screen readers
Reduced-motion option for sparkline animations and cost microchip transitions
review_notes: PM (Ravi Patel) asked for a clearer separation between transient pool alerts and long-term health trends
Engineering (Sofia Ivanov) suggested moving 'Instant test' burst runs to a job queue to avoid spiking control-plane load
Security (Liam O'Connor) requested audit hooks for policy changes and a confirmation step for role-bound edits
Design critique: add a compact help tooltip that describes 'burst credits' and links to billing docs
acceptance_criteria: Design has developer-facing handoff with annotated Figma frames and a CSS token map
Accessibility checklist completed and signed off by Accessibility SME
Engineering review meeting completed with clear API usage notes and a stubbed endpoint for cost simulation
Clickable prototype validated in two usability sessions with Platform SREs and at least 3 actionable improvements captured
next_steps: Incorporate engineering feedback around test-run throttling and update prototype flows
Prepare handoff packet: annotated Figma + icon exports + interaction spec
Schedule dev design pairing sessions during Cycle 2025-W10
Create a short demo video for internal docs and on-call training
